hypothesis: If crayfish or lobsters (Aristotle's Carabi) and some crabs have a second set of teeth in the stomach, then a comparative foregut survey will describe a gastric mill, median tooth or lateral teeth for at least one crayfish or lobster and for at least one crab or for brachyurans as a group.
pass_criterion: At least one name in the Carabi list is scored present, and at least one name in the crab list or the word Brachyura is scored present.
fail_criterion: Every mentioned Carabi name is scored absent, or crabs are discussed and every crab name and Brachyura are scored absent. If Carabi names are present and crab names are absent, the verdict is mixed. If no Carabi name occurs in the text, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable. The adaptive 'because the front teeth are insufficient' clause is not part of the verdict; it is recorded as untested.
interpretation: Carabi are crayfish and lobsters: Cambarus, Astacus, Homarus, Nephrops, Panulirus, Palinurus, Procambarus, Cherax, Jasus, Euastacus, Orconectes, Faxonius. Crabs are Cancer, Carcinus, Callinectes, Uca, Portunus, Maja, Xantho, Pachygrapsus, plus the group name Brachyura. 'A second set of teeth in the stomach' is the gastric mill: median tooth, lateral teeth, or the mill named as such. A complex foregut ossicle system in that group counts as present. Mouthpart teeth do not count.

test_contract.expected_observation: The survey describes stomach teeth or a gastric mill in at least one crayfish or lobster and in at least one crab group.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: The survey says the gastric mill is absent in the crayfish and lobsters it examines, or absent in the crabs it examines.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: A publicly downloadable comparative anatomical text that examines decapod foreguts and names genera or the brachyuran group. A single-species note that does not mention both a carabus and a crab cannot pass both halves.
test_contract.inference_method: From the extracted text, a name is present if it occurs within 250 characters of 'gastric mill', 'median tooth', 'lateral teeth', 'gastric teeth' or 'ossicle' and that window does not say the mill is absent, lacking or missing. A name is absent if it occurs within 250 characters of 'no gastric mill', 'lacks a gastric mill', 'without a gastric mill' or 'gastric mill is absent'. Group scores follow the pass and fail rules.
